en.bdb: Living up to one's natural repute

verses.gurmukhi: ਪਾਣੀ ਕਾਠੁ ਨ ਡੋਬਈ ਪਾਲੇ ਦੀ ਲਜੈ।
verses.translit_en: paanee kaaTh na ddobiee paale dhee lajai|

en.bdb: Water does not drown the wood because it lives up to its natural repute of nurturing the things (water rears up the vegetation).

verses.gurmukhi: ਸਿਰਿ ਕਲਵਤ੍ਰ ਧਰਾਇਕੈ ਸਿਰਿ ਚੜਿਆ ਭਜੈ।
verses.translit_en: sir kalavatr dharaikai sir chaRiaa bhajai|

en.bdb: It bears the vessel on its head like a saw because the vessel shears the water and moves ahead.

verses.gurmukhi: ਲੋਹੇ ਜੜੀਐ ਬੋਹਿਥਾ ਭਾਰਿ ਭਰੇ ਨ ਤਜੈ।
verses.translit_en: lohe jaReeaai bohithaa bhaar bhare na tajai|

en.bdb: Of course, iron is studded into the wood but water bears the burden of it also.

verses.gurmukhi: ਪੇਟੈ ਅੰਦਰਿ ਅਗਿ ਰਖਿ ਤਿਸੁ ਪੜਦਾ ਕਜੈ।
verses.translit_en: peTai a(n)dhar ag rakh tis paRadhaa kajai|

en.bdb: Water knows that its enemy fire exists in wood but still it covers up this fact and does not drown it.

verses.gurmukhi: ਅਗਰੈ ਡੋਬੈ ਜਾਣਿ ਕੈ ਨਿਰਮੋਲਕ ਧਜੈ।
verses.translit_en: agarai ddobai jaan kai niramolak dhajai|

en.bdb: The sandal wood is knowingly drowned so that it is proved to be the real sandal wood and its price may be fixed higher.

verses.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਮਾਰਗਿ ਚਲਣਾ ਛਡਿ ਖਬੈ ਸਜੈ ॥੧੫॥
verses.translit_en: gurmukh maarag chalanaa chhadd khabai sajai ||15||

en.bdb: The way of the gurmukhs is also the same; they without the caring for the loss and the profit go on moving further and further.
